File mtimes on all four files (2026-07-29 12:07:24-12:42:47 +09:00) predate the freeze commit (12:49:12 +09:00) and have survived unchanged through many later commits, which is only possible if git never had to rewrite them on checkout. The frozen module `src/rabbit/decoupling/_independent_noqke.py` hashes to 760a7c044081e507fae9d5695b301bd44f6466d96322c46f53b77161e32b558a, matching the value pinned in the working notes and embedded as `module_sha256`/`MODULE_SHA256` in the banked report and driver, and the driver checks this hash itself at startup (exiting 30 on mismatch). findings.statement: The '11051 evaluations' figure for the domain-holdout phase, stated as a specific fact in both the ce737a7 commit message and the VALIDATION_LEDGER.md row, is stated at a precision the retained bytes do not support and is most likely a modest understatement of the true final count. Because the wall-budget TimeoutError fired inside domain-phase run_integration, `report['domain_holdout']` was never assigned (the exception unwinds before that line in main()), so the banked JSON report carries no domain-phase eval count at all: it has no 'domain_holdout' key, and the literal substring '11051' does not appear anywhere in the file except as a coincidental fragment inside two unrelated long decimals (lines 4509 and 8743, e.g. '...105117...'). The only source for '11051' is the stdout log's last periodic progress line, '[ 64718.9s] eval 11051: N=0.1653 ...', which by construction is quantized to multiples of 50 (the driver logs only when stats.evals % 50 == 1). The run continued for a further 83.0 s after that line (64801.9 - 64718.9) before the deadline check in the next RHS call raised TimeoutError, and the measured per-eval cost in that same regime is ~4.42-4.49 s/eval (e.g. (64718.9-15860.7)/11051 = 4.4211 s/eval using the domain-phase start line, or ~4.49 s/eval using recent local windows within the trace). At that rate, roughly 15-20 further complete RHS evaluations most plausibly occurred in the unlogged 83.0 s gap, none of which would appear at a %50 checkpoint, putting the true final count closer to ~11065-11070 than to exactly 11051. Both documents state '11051 evaluations' without any qualifying language ('at least', 'last logged at'), presenting a lower-bound/checkpoint value as if it were the exact terminal count. This does not change the qualitative conclusion (N advances by roughly 2.3e-7 per eval in this stalled regime, so even 20 more evaluations move the reported N by an amount far below the quoted 4-decimal precision) and does not affect any gated verdict, since T13 was never evaluated in this run. It does, however, mean this one specific number in an otherwise scrupulously self-consistent report/commit/ledger triad cannot itself be independently reconstructed to the stated precision from the retained bytes -- precisely the class of defect (a reported number not recoverable from retained state) that the D-065 finding and this run's own T14 predicate were designed to eliminate.
assumptions_used: deadline.check() is called exactly once per RHS invocation, at the top of _trajectory_core.py's rhs() closure, and stats.evals increments once per completed RHS call after that check passes -- confirmed by direct code read, not merely inferred.

The measured local per-eval cost in the final third of the domain-holdout trace (~4.4-4.5 s/eval) is representative of the unlogged 83.0 s gap immediately following it; there is no evidence of a sudden per-eval slowdown/speedup at that exact boundary, but this is an extrapolation, not a directly retained figure.

findings.statement: artifacts/OPERATOR_OBSERVATION_domain_holdout_stall.json is consistent with the final banked report and with the no-intervention claim, and is independently corroborated by filesystem mtimes. Its embedded domain_holdout_trace (evals 1-1501, N oscillating 0.1628/0.1813/0.1629 from eval 351 onward) is a strict, uninterrupted prefix of the same stdout log later banked in ce737a7: the trace's timestamps and N values at evals 1, 51, ..., 1501 match r4_trajectory_stdout.log exactly, and the same oscillation-then-crawl pattern continues (N settling near 0.164-0.165) all the way to the final logged eval 11051, consistent with 'not slow, stopped' rather than an artifact of the sampling window chosen for the mid-run note. Its head_commit 'd94270fecedb3b6dca7276f27bae91da348cdf16' is a real, verifiable commit (2026-07-29T10:05:09Z, 'fix(harness): close the round-5 findings...') that landed on this branch 177 seconds before the observation's own recorded_at (2026-07-29T10:08:06Z), confirming ordinary D-070 harness-development work continued in parallel on the branch during the run -- exactly the parallel-axis pattern this project has separately authorized -- without touching any of the four frozen r4 files (independently confirmed in F-001). Strong independent corroboration of 'no intervention': the banked report file's on-disk mtime is 2026-07-30T06:49:28+09:00 = 2026-07-29T21:49:28Z, identical to the second to the report's own internal 'completed_at' field; the banked stdout log's mtime is 2026-07-30T06:48:05+09:00 = 2026-07-29T21:48:05Z, matching started_at (03:49:26Z) + the log's own final elapsed-time bracket (64718.9s) to within the same second (03:49:26 + 64718.9s = 21:48:04.9Z). Two independently-sourced timestamps (git-checkout-surviving filesystem mtimes, on a host whose timezone Asia/Seoul matches the +09:00 offset used throughout) agree with the internal report/log timestamps to the second, which would be very unlikely to occur if either artifact had been edited, regenerated, or backdated after the fact.
assumptions_used: Filesystem mtimes reflect the last write time of the file content and were not reset by an intervening `git checkout`/`touch` that happened to coincidentally reproduce the exact internal timestamps; the second-level agreement across two independently-computed internal quantities (an absolute UTC field and a start+elapsed-seconds sum) makes coincidence very unlikely but is not a formal proof.

findings.statement: OPERATOR_OBSERVATION_domain_holdout_stall.json's own 'measured_cost_note' field ('60/30 ran at 4.275 s/eval, against the contract's unbacked assertion of 4.754 s/eval') does not reconstruct from its own embedded domain_holdout_trace. Using the trace's own anchor points -- domain-phase start (t=15860.7s, from the stdout header line, equal to consumed_at_observation_s's frame of reference) through the trace's own final row (t=22542.2s, eval=1501) -- the implied rate is (22542.2-15860.7)/1501 = 4.4514 s/eval, or (22542.2-15865.2)/1500 = 4.4513 s/eval using the first logged eval as the anchor; recent-local-window estimates within the same trace (e.g. eval 951->1501) give ~4.49-4.50 s/eval. None of these reconstructions land near 4.275, and no other derivation basis in the retained trace produces that figure. The eventual full-phase average, correctly computed in the final ce737a7 commit and ledger row as 4.4287 s/eval, is consistent with the trace-derived ~4.45-4.49 s/eval range, which further underscores that 4.275 is the outlier. This is a narrow, low-impact defect: the artifact is explicitly labeled 'OPERATOR_OBSERVATION_NOT_EVIDENCE', its 4.275 figure is not repeated anywhere in the final report, commit message, or ledger row (all of which independently and correctly compute 4.4287 s/eval from the full-phase bytes, per F-002), and it does not affect any T-predicate, gate, or verdict. It is nonetheless a genuine, reproducible internal inconsistency in a document whose stated purpose is honest contemporaneous observation, and it directly answers 'is the OPERATOR_OBSERVATION artifact ... consistent with the final report' with a qualified no on this one sub-field.
assumptions_used: consumed_at_observation_s (22542.2) and the trace's own t_s values share the same time origin as the domain-phase start line in the stdout log (both are elapsed seconds since the driver's own process start); this is the natural reading given consumed_at_observation_s equals the trace's own last t_s exactly.
counterevidence_refs: An alternative computation basis unavailable in the retained bytes (e.g. an internal EWMA or a window predating the retained trace) could in principle produce 4.275; no such basis could be identified from what is retained.
unresolved: The exact derivation the mid-run observer used to arrive at 4.275 s/eval is not retained anywhere and could not be reverse-engineered from the available evidence.

findings.statement: Testing the strongest alternative reading of the wall-budget breach (that the 1.9 s overshoot is a coordinator-favourable framing of a run that was going to fail its gates anyway): the overshoot magnitude itself is fully explained mechanically and is not evidence of favourable tuning. `Deadline.check()` (_trajectory_core.py:61-73) is called exactly once, at the very top of the RHS closure (_trajectory_core.py:182), before any per-eval work; breach-detection latency is therefore bounded by the duration of one full RHS evaluation. At the domain phase's own measured cost (~4.4-4.5 s/eval, F-002/F-003), a 1.9 s overshoot is well under one eval-interval -- an unremarkable, expected consequence of coarse per-eval polling, not a suspiciously precise near-miss. The 'breach is mechanical, never a scientific verdict' framing itself is not post-hoc: it is written verbatim in the frozen contract (docs/audit/BD622_D069_independent_trajectory_r4_contract_2026-07-29.md section 7, 'breach is a mechanical exit 20, never a scientific verdict... a breach yields no checks block at all'), committed at 0fb94f2 before the run produced a single output byte, so this is a pre-registered interpretive choice rather than a rationalization invented after seeing the outcome. What the retained evidence CANNOT settle: (i) whether a differently-designed, finer-grained deadline check would have produced a materially different exit point or (in principle) let T13 actually evaluate before the budget ran out -- this is inherent to the chosen once-per-RHS-call check granularity and is not recoverable from the bytes; (ii) a rigorous proof that the domain-holdout companion would never reach its terminal condition given materially more wall-clock time -- the commit's 'not slow, it is stopped' framing is a strong, well-supported extrapolation (net N-drift of only ~2.3e-7 per eval over the final ~10700 evaluations, oscillating rather than trending, which at the observed local rate would require several more orders of magnitude of additional evaluations to close the remaining ~7.77 in N) but it remains an extrapolation from an ~11000-eval sample, not a convergence proof. On balance the retained evidence supports 'this configuration was not going to finish within any practically reachable extension of an 18 h class budget' considerably better than it supports either the literal claim of permanent non-convergence or the alternative hypothesis of favourable framing; neither of the latter two is fully settleable from the bytes alone.
assumptions_used: The per-eval RHS cost in the unobserved final 83.0 s of the run was similar to the measured cost in the preceding hours of the same phase (no retained evidence of a discontinuity, but also none ruling one out).

findings.statement: The claim of bitwise identity to the preserved r3, r2 and D-056 base endpoints is TRUE at full float64 precision across the whole retained endpoint block, spectra, blocks and residual rows -- not only across the four scalars (N_eff, N_end, t_end_s, evals) literally quoted in the commit message. A recursive Python dict-diff of r4['base'] against r3['base'] and r2['base'] finds zero VALUE_DIFF entries anywhere in the overlapping keys (the only differences are MISSING_IN_A/MISSING_IN_B entries from keys r4 renamed or added relative to r3/r2, e.g. r4's new 'checkpoint_states'/'spectral'/'setup' vs r3/r2's 'spectrum_sup_rel'/'spectrum_sup_rel_full'/'spectrum_subsupport_nodes'). Direct `==` equality (Python, hence bit-identical) holds between r4 and r3/r2 for: the full 'endpoint' dict (N_eff, N_end, T_cm_end, T_gamma_end, evals, gamma_heating_ratio, t_end_s), 'blocks' (rho_nu, n_e, rho_e, n_x, rho_x, split_ratio), 'residual_rows', 'max_R_total' (6.965641112523105e-05 in all three), 'max_roundoff' (0.0 in all three), 'rejections' (count/final/max/min identical), 'tail_last_node_fraction' (1.2430778875527049e-08 in all three), and all four 48-element spectrum arrays f_e/f_mu/f_tau/grid_nodes. r4's endpoint dict also equals D-056's top-level 'endpoint' dict field-for-field on every key D-056 retained (D-056 lacks only the 'evals' field, which the other two runs have). This is corroborated by identical numpy/scipy versions across r4/r3/r2 (2.4.4/1.17.1) and by the confirmed-correct BLAS single-thread pinning in the banked driver (F-001) -- multi-threaded BLAS would make bit-identical reduction order across independent runs implausible, so the fact that bit-identity does hold is itself indirect evidence the pinning fix is doing its job.

errors.description: The first submission of this envelope declared top-level status=pass while simultaneously carrying finding verdicts fail (F-003), fail (F-005), and inconclusive (F-006). The real project SubagentStop hook correctly blocked admission with 'Result artifact violates RESULT_ENVELOPE: status=pass requires every finding verdict to be pass' and the admission receipt was left open. That was a self-inconsistency in the envelope, not a change of substance: none of the seven findings' statements, evidence, or verdicts were altered to produce this correction. The only changes made in response are (1) top-level status corrected from 'pass' to 'fail' -- the honest aggregate given that F-003 and F-005 are verified, reproducible defects (not merely suspicions) and F-006 is a genuine inconclusive on a question the retained bytes cannot fully settle, so a blanket 'pass' misrepresented the audit's own findings; (2) completed_at updated to a fresh real `date -u` stamp captured at the moment of this correction; (3) this error record added. The substantive conclusion is unchanged: no refit, no post-hoc selection, no fabrication, and no gate manipulation were found anywhere in the D-069 r4 banking commit ce737a7; the fail/inconclusive verdicts are confined to two low-materiality precision/sourcing gaps (F-003, F-005) and one epistemically-limited framing question (F-006), none of which move any gate or contradict the mechanical-ERROR characterization.
